articles.title: Golden Goose Teams With Disney for Mickey Mouse-Inspired Sneakers, Apparel and Global Customization Tour
articles.summary: Golden Goose is teaming up with Disney for a new Mickey & Friends collection, featuring the Italian luxury brand’s signature distressed sneakers alongside a lineup of apparel and accessories inspired by the iconic animated characters. Launching Oct.
body: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

The collection also includes Disney-themed patches, pins, charms and embellished laces, allowing shoppers to put their own spin on the designs. Through Golden Goose’s signature Co-Creation experience, customers can further customize select pieces with screen-printed Disney graphics.

The collaboration extends beyond the merchandise with a worldwide Co-Creation tour featuring Disney character artists and Golden Goose’s in-house artisans, known as Dream Makers. During the in-store events, Disney artists will personalize Golden Goose products with character designs and create live Mickey & Friends illustrations on co-branded cards for guests to take home.

Fans can also take part in Disney-inspired workshops, including creating Mickey Mouse ears, coloring comic-book illustrations and designing custom keychains. A special co-branded Mickey & Friends balloon will also be available as a gift.

articles.title: Cannes Queer Animated Comedy ‘Jim Queen’ Scores New Sales at Busan (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Cannes animated comedy “Jim Queen” has picked up a new batch of international sales after screening at the Busan International Film Festival, its first outing in Asia.
body: For the U.S., Global Constellation is weighing several offers, with a release set for 2027. Jordan Firstman and Matteo Lane were recently unveiled as the English-language voices of Jim and Lucien.

Set in Paris, the story centers on Jim, a gym-obsessed influencer and the most desired man on the city’s gay scene. His status collapses overnight when a strange virus called Heterosis begins converting gay men to heterosexuality. Dropped by his followers and shunned by his circle, Jim has only Lucien on his side, a skinny and fiercely loyal admirer. The pair head into the Marais in search of a renegade doctor who may hold a cure.

The film world premiered at Cannes, where festival chief Thierry Frémaux called the screening “one of the most beautiful in the festival’s history in terms of atmosphere.” The Jokers Films opened it in France on June 17, and it entered the box office chart at No. 3 behind “Toy Story 5” and “Backrooms.” It has since passed 385,000 admissions there and taken more than $3 million.

body: In the film, Thị Mầu is a gifted young beauty hemmed in by rigid custom and the demands of her family. The film will open in Vietnamese cinemas at the end of October, with 3388 Films’ theatrical rollout across several continents set to follow later this year.

articles.title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
articles.summary: Mitte, who lived with cerebral palsy, starred as Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series.
body: US actor RJ Mitte, best known for his role as the defiant son of drug kingpin Walter White in the drama series Breaking Bad, has died aged 34.
"It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," his representative told the BBC.
He died in Brownsville, Texas. No immediate cause of death was provided.
"Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," his representative, Sean Reilly, said in a statement to the BBC.

articles.title: BBC shelves plans for new Archers studio as part of cost-cutting
articles.summary: The drama has been recording in Birmingham for 75 years, making it the world's longest running soap opera.
body: The BBC has shelved plans to build a new bespoke studio for The Archers in Birmingham as part of its wider drive to cut costs, opening up the possibility it could be recorded outside of the city for the first time.
The world's longest-running soap opera, The Archers has been recording in the West Midlands city for 75 years.
The BBC had initially pledged to build the show a new studio in the Tea Factory, the corporation's new hub in Digbeth, central Birmingham.
The broadcaster said it was "currently assessing the BBC's existing studio facilities around the UK as well as other external studio options in the West Midlands".

articles.title: Alex Gibney says Universal ‘wavered’ over releasing Elon Musk documentary
articles.summary: The revelation comes after the four-hour film’s Venice premiere drew a string of criticisms and insults from the founder of SpaceXAI. Alex Gibney, director of the new four-hour documentary about Elon Musk, said that Universal, owners of the film’s international distribution rights “wavered” over…
body: Gibney was speaking to the New York Times as the film opened in the US (where it is being released by the independent distributor Bleecker Street), and appeared to confirm a story in the Hollywood Reporter that Universal, which had acquired the international rights to the film in 2023, had got cold feet. Asked by the New York Times, “Did Universal Pictures waver in setting up its international release plans?” Gibney replied: “Yes.”

A subsequent story in Variety suggested that Universal had been concerned about “legal threats from Musk”, but that the studio had “always been enthusiastic about releasing the film internationally”. Gibney was asked: “So it wasn’t about legal clearances?” The film-maker replied: “You can walk and chew gum at the same time.”
However, it appears plans are back on track, as Gibney added: “We just had a meeting with [Universal], and we’re talking very concretely about a release plan.”

articles.title: US actress Selma Blair accused of assault after incident with flight attendants
articles.summary: The Legally Blonde star is investigated by the FBI following an alleged altercation on a flight from LA to New York.
body: US actress Selma Blair has been issued with a summons accusing her of assault after she allegedly attacked attendants on a plane, officials say.
The Legally Blonde star was investigated by the FBI following an alleged altercation on a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to New York.

Airport officials said they had responded to a call on Sunday about "a physically abusive passenger" on the flight. Two flight attendants were hurt and one was taken to hospital, the New York Port Authority said.
Blair, 54, who also starred in Hellboy and Cruel Intentions, was arrested and taken to hospital. Her publicist told the BBC she had "experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct".

articles.title: Digger on course for $245m loss after box office collapse
articles.summary: Estimates suggest the eco satire starring Tom Cruise could join the list of top turkeys, including Cutthroat Island and The Marvels. Digger, the ambitious eco-fable starring Tom Cruise and directed by Alejandro G Iñárritu, is heading for an even worse financial outcome than previously thought, with…
body: According to a report in Variety, Digger’s estimated second weekend revenue in North America of $3.2m is a 60% drop on its opening weekend figure of $8m, meaning its current domestic gross is $14.4m, for a global total of $35.3m, with a projected final box office total of around $50m worldwide.
A $245m loss would put Digger on a par with such legendary turkeys as Cutthroat Island ($222m loss, adjusted for inflation), Mortal Engines ($224m adjusted) and The Marvels ($205-$250m adjusted).

Reaction to the film has likely played a key role in its underperformance, with critical opinion radically divided. In the Guardian, chief film critic Peter Bradshaw called it “an exasperatingly shallow, laborious, self-congratulatory satire” in a two-star review, while Guardian Australia’s deputy culture editor Sian Cain took the opposite position, describing it as “a masterpiece”. Warner Bros, whose last release this is before its takeover by David Ellison’s Skydance, tried to play into the controversy with a post-release advertising campaign quoting its negative notices, but it seems to have had little effect.

articles.title: Hallowarrior review – apocalyptic Home Alone-style survival horror delivers inventive shocks
articles.summary: Debut feature from Ben Sottak provides outlandish Halloween-based scares, with Milly Shapiro superb as the naive yet resilient home-defender, Pumpkin. Home Alone meets Mad Max in this atmospheric seasonal chiller, named for Halloween and not a cheery greeting.
body: It’s the first major screen role for Shapiro since her memorable debut as the little sister in Ari Aster’s Hereditary, and she is in almost every scene here, making for quite the showcase. It’s good casting: Pumpkin is an intriguing presence – at once young and old, presumably because she’s been fending for herself during such a key stage of her development. She’s not had any adult guidance since the age of 12 – arresting her development in some ways, while having to survive, be totally independent and grieve her entire family alone has simultaneously made her unusually tough in others.

articles.title: ‘Ink’ Finally Meets Its Native Audience at London Film Festival, and Jack O’Connell Has Thoughts
articles.summary: Guy Pearce and director Danny Boyle also stopped to talk to The Hollywood Reporter about bringing Rupert Murdoch's Fleet Street origin story to U.K. fans: "If it doesn't work here, it's not going to work anywhere."
body: Danny Boyle and his starry cast, led by Jack O’Connell and Guy Pearce, took to the BFI London Film Festival carpet for the U.K. premiere on Monday night, around a month after it opened the Venice Film Festival.

The movie, adapted from James Graham’s stage play, depicts Pearce’s Rupert Murdoch as he enters the British newspaper scene, acquiring the then-failing tabloid The Sun in 1969. Hiring Larry Lamb (O’Connell) as editor, the two combined far-right political reporting and populist rabble to turn the paper into a dark force in British media. Murdoch would take the lessons learned at The Sun and apply them to build his U.S. media empire with The New York Post and Fox News.

Backdropped by the smoky, seedy journalistic epicentre that is Fleet Street, O’Connell said he didn’t categorize the notorious Lamb as a “bad” person. “I think he was just perhaps overly ambitious,” said the star. “I think this guy was on a pursuit, or his obsession was newspapers, and I guess he broke a couple of rules along the way. And it wasn’t victimless, but yeah, I don’t consider him an out-and-out bad guy.”
